frontMatter.introduction:
Welcome to the Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) Manual for Agrawal Metal Works Pvt. Ltd. Since our establishment in 1945, Agrawal Metal Works has adhered to a philosophy of excellence, dedicated to being best-in-class for our customers. We take pride in our position as a leading manufacturer of Copper and Copper Alloy Foils, Strips, and Sheets, as well as Copper and Brass Round and Flatted Wires and Fine Grain Brass Ingots in India.

As we continue to expand our presence in the Indian and international markets, we recognize the importance of integrating sustainability into our core business practices. This manual serves as a comprehensive framework to guide our commitment to environmental stewardship, social responsibility, and robust governance.

By embedding ESG principles into our operations, we aim to minimize our environmental impact, enhance the welfare of our employees and communities, and uphold the highest standards of ethical conduct. Through this manual, we seek to promote a culture of sustainability, accountability, and transparency, ensuring that Agrawal Metal Works remains a trusted partner for our stakeholders and a leader in our industry.

Promoting sustainability, enhancing community engagement, and ensuring ethical practices--this manual serves as a comprehensive guide for embedding Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) considerations into the core operations of Agrawal Metal Works Pvt. Ltd., supporting our mission for responsible business conduct.
frontMatter.scope: The ESG SOP Manual applies to all operations and activities related to environmental management, social responsibility, and governance practices and is applicable to all employees contractors, third-party vendors, and stakeholders involved in the operations of Agrawal Metal Works Pvt. Ltd. It includes guidelines for minimizing environmental impact, promoting employee welfare, ensuring ethical conduct, and engaging with stakeholders.

sections.title: Procedure for Recovering Material from Dross

blocks.text: Efficiently recovering and recycling valuable materials from dross generated during the metal production process, thereby minimizing waste and promoting resource sustainability.

sections.title: Procedure for Recovering Material from Dross

body.text: Waste Management Team collects dross bins from all production lines and records the weight of each bin during collection.
The collected dross is allowed to cool down before further handling. safety measures are in place while handling hot materials must be ensured.

After cooling, larger metal lumps are segregated from the remaining fine dross. The large lumps are set aside for further processing which includes crushing or shredding, melting, fluxing, separation, cooling and solidifying, recycling.
The remaining fine dross is collected and processed using a pulverizer. Safety protocols are followed during the operation must be ensured.
The fine segregated dross is charged into the pulverizer hopper, ensuring it is clear of obstructions.
The pulverizer grinds the dross. The grinding process is monitored for efficiency, ensuring that ash and dust are collected in the bag filter.
Recovery of Materials
The recovered metal particles are utilized in the casting process, ensuring to track the quantity used for inventory purposes.
Any losses during the process, which are estimated to be between 0.5% to 0.9% are documented. This record will be useful for process evaluation and improvement.

sections.title: Procedure for Managing Hazardous Substances: Labeling, Storing, Handling, and Transporting

blocks.text: To establish guidelines for the safe labeling, storing, handling, and transporting of hazardous substances to protect employee health, safety, and the environment.

sections.title: Procedure for Managing Hazardous Substances: Labeling, Storing, Handling, and Transporting

steps.heading: Unloading and Storage of Hazardous Substances

body.text: Unload Material: Hazardous substances are carefully unloaded from trucks by first verifying shipping documents and inspecting the unloading area for safety. Personnel wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE), and a signal person is designated to coordinate movements. Proper manual handling techniques or mechanical aids, such as forklifts, are used for heavier loads while checking containers for damage and verifying received quantities. Once unloaded, the containers are transported to designated storage areas, maintaining cleanliness in the unloading zone. The shipping documents typically verified during the unloading of hazardous substances include:

Bill of Lading (BOL)
Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS)
Packing List
Hazardous Materials Declaration
Import/Export Permits

Verification: The quantity and type of hazardous substances are verified by cross-checking the bill of lading, Material Safety Data Sheets, and packing lists for accuracy, along with validating the Hazardous Materials Declaration and any required permits to ensure compliance with safety regulations, before moving them to designated storage areas.

Hazardous substances are stored in designated areas based on their specific classifications, ensuring that each container is clearly labeled with its contents and associated hazards. The storage area remains locked and secured to prevent unauthorized access, protecting personnel and maintaining safety protocols

All hazardous substances are labeled in accordance with the Globally Harmonized System (GHS). Below given table provides a clear overview of the labeling requirements based on the Globally Harmonized System (GHS).

Spill Response: In the event of a spill, employees immediately execute spill response procedures, including evacuating the area and employing absorbent materials for containment and cleanup. All spills are promptly reported to a supervisor, and incidents are documented according to company reporting guidelines.

Hazardous waste is disposed of through licensed waste disposal contractors at approved facilities, ensuring compliance with local, state, and federal regulations. The responsibility for managing hazardous waste disposal lies with the Environmental Health and Safety Officer, who oversees the selection of contractors and ensures proper classification and packaging of the waste.

Documents must be retained for record-keeping and regulatory compliance. The disposal methods employed may include incineration, treatment, or secure landfilling, depending on the type of hazardous waste.

All hazardous substances are securely packaged in compliance with applicable regulations to prevent leaks during transportation.
Packaging includes appropriate labeling that adheres to the Globally Harmonized System (GHS) for safe handling.
Containers specifically designed to contain hazardous substances are utilized to minimize the risk of spillage.
Vehicles used for transportation are equipped with necessary safety features, including secondary containment systems and spill kits.
Proper ventilation must be ensured within transport vehicles to handle hazardous materials safely.
Drivers receive specialized training on the handling and transport of hazardous substances.
Transport routes are pre-planned to avoid densely populated areas whenever possible.
Regular inspections of both packaging and vehicles are conducted to ensure integrity and compliance with safety standards.
All employees involved in the handling, storage, and transportation of hazardous substances must receive training on this procedure and the hazards associated with the materials they work with.

blocks.text: To implement measures that minimize the spill of oil and grease during operations, thereby reducing environmental impact and ensuring workplace safety.

sections.title: Procedure to minimize spill of oil and grease at various levels of work

body.text: Before transporting oil or grease from the stores to the user department, the store personnel checks that the cap of the drum is properly sealed to prevent any spillage during shifting.
The drum is shifted using a forklift or trolley by warehouse staff, as manual handling is prohibited to avoid injuries and spillage.

steps.heading: Placing the drum in designated area

body.text: Upon arrival, the drum is placed in the designated area, such as the Oil Room, by warehouse staff to ensure proper storage and access.
Oil is transferred from the drum into a pouring pot by maintenance personnel using a hand-operated pump and funnel.
A tray or suitable vessel is used by maintenance personnel to collect any drained-out oil during the transfer process.
When topping up the gearbox with fresh oil, maintenance personnel utilize a funnel to minimize the risk of spillage.
Used oil is stored in a designated waste oil drum by maintenance personnel.
The drum is returned to the stores department by warehouse staff with a completed return voucher to ensure proper tracking and disposal.

blocks.text:
Purpose
To establish guidelines for the effective operation and maintenance of the Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP) to ensure the treatment of wastewater meets regulatory standards and minimizes environmental impact.

body.text:
All personnel including operations team, maintenance team, environmental compliance officer, safety officers conduct visual inspections of equipment and surrounding areas of their respective concern daily before starting operations.
The checks and replenishments of chemical levels are performed by the operations team, while the regular inspections of fire extinguishers, eyewash stations, and other safety equipment are conducted by safety officers.

Influent Monitoring: The influent flow rate is measured using flow meters. Operators record parameters such as pH, temperature, total suspended solids (TSS), and biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) to ensure proper treatment.
Chemical Dosing: Based on the influent characteristics, dosing pumps are used to adjust the chemical dosage. Operators document the dosages and any adjustments made.
Process Monitoring: Regular inspections of treatment units are performed by the Operations Team to ensure optimal operation. The aeration levels in aeration tanks are monitored and adjusted as needed. Clarifiers are inspected for performance, and sludge levels are controlled regularly.
Effluent Testing: Effluent samples are collected at designated points. Key parameters such as pH, TSS, BOD, chemical oxygen demand (COD), and other specific contaminants are tested by the laboratory technicians as per permit requirements. Results are recorded and compared with regulatory limits by the operations team. Below is a table summarizing the effluent testing parameters:

In case of non-compliance, the laboratory technicians notify the Environmental Compliance Officer, who investigates and implements corrective actions such as adjusting chemical dosages, modifying operational parameters, conducting maintenance on equipment, retraining personnel on procedures, and increasing monitoring frequency to ensure compliance with regulatory standards. The incident is documented in the logbook, and additional monitoring is conducted to ensure compliance.

Operators clean all equipment and work areas daily after operations.
Standard shutdown procedures are followed to power down the plant equipment safely.
All daily data that includes daily operational data such as influent and effluent parameters, maintenance activities including dates and descriptions of work performed, sample analysis results, compliance reports, and any incidents or observations noted during the operations are logged accurately for future reference.

sections.title: C. Procedures for the reduction in water consumption

blocks.text:
Purpose
To establish strategies and practices for reducing water consumption at Agrawal Metal Works, enhancing operational efficiency while promoting sustainability and environmental stewardship.

sections.title: C. Procedures for the reduction in water consumption - Procedure

steps.heading: Optimizing Water Usage and Wastewater Generation

body.text:
Regular assessments of water usage are conducted by the Maintenance Team and Environmental Compliance Officer to identify areas for improvement in maintenance, surface treatment, and equipment sanitation activities.
High-pressure washing systems are utilized in processes such as equipment cleaning, surface preparation, vehicle washing, and industrial facility cleaning to minimize water consumption during cleaning operations. Also, In deburring processes, optimized water jets are employed that utilize less water while effectively removing burrs, ensuring minimal wastewater generation.
Only biodegradable cleaning agents, such as citrus-based cleaners, plant-based surfactants, vinegar and baking soda mixtures, that require less water for rinsing are employed. These agents effectively clean surfaces while minimizing environmental impact.
Closed-loop systems are utilized in various manufacturing as well as finishing operations such as roller mills and deburring, electrolytic stripping and rinsing after coating, to recirculate water, hence minimizing wastewater generation and conserving resources. This system is regularly monitored to ensure its effectiveness and efficiency.

steps.responsible: Maintenance Team and Environmental Compliance Officer

body.text:
Monthly visual inspections of water supply lines and bi-weekly checks for cooling systems are conducted
Acoustic leak detection equipment and flow monitoring systems are utilized for identifying and locating leaks in water supply systems, ensuring timely repairs, and minimizing water loss.
Upon detecting a leak, the water supply is immediately shut off to prevent further damage. The situation is then evaluated by the maintenance team to determine the extent of the issue, followed by the performance of necessary repairs. After the repairs are completed, the area is monitored closely by the maintenance team to ensure that no further leaks occur.

Gutters and downpipes have been installed on designated roof areas to efficiently channel rainwater into storage tanks.
A first flush system is in place to divert initial runoff, ensuring only cleaner rainwater enters the storage tanks.
Harvested rainwater is stored in covered tanks and used for non-potable applications such as irrigation and cooling processes.
Regular inspections and cleaning of the collection system, filters, and tanks are conducted by the maintainance team to maintain system efficiency.
Water levels and usage are continuously tracked, and data is recorded to measure water savings and system performance.

The performance of water-efficient cooling towers is continuously monitored using flow meters and temperature sensors to ensure optimal operation.
Continuous monitoring of cooling tower performance using flow meters and temperature sensors is conducted to ensure optimal operation.
Routine inspections and cleaning of cooling towers and associated systems are conducted to maintain efficiency and prevent buildup of contaminants.
Acoustic leak detection equipment is utilized, and any identified leaks are immediately repaired to minimize water loss and ensure system integrity.
Detailed records of water usage, maintenance activities, and performance metrics are regularly documented and reviewed for continuous improvement.

blocks.text: To implement effective strategies and measures to monitor, control, and reduce air pollution emissions from Agrawal Metal Works, ensuring compliance with environmental regulations and promoting a healthier workplace and community.

body.text: Installation of Control Technologies: Wet scrubbers are installed at furnance exhaust system and Solvent recovery system to capture and remove gaseous pollutants such as VOCs and SOx from exhaust streams before they are released into the atmosphere. Fixed bed adsorbers utilizing activated carbon are employed to trap VOCs and heavy metals from air emissions, ensuring their effective removal.

Regular Maintenance and Monitoring: The installed emission control equipment, including scrubbers and adsorption systems, undergoes regular inspections to ensure optimal performance and efficiency. Continuous Emissions Monitoring Systems (CEMS), including gas analyzers for SO, NOx, CO, and particulate matter (PM), are installed at emission points to track pollutants in real-time. These systems are maintained and calibrated regularly to ensure accurate readings. Air samples are collected quaterly by an external, approved laboratory for detailed analysis. The samples are tested for compliance with regulatory standards for air quality.
The air samples are tested for key parameters including

rows: Fine particles that affect respiratory health
Gas contributing to acid rain and respiratory issues
Major air pollutant from combustion processes
Toxic gas produced by incomplete combustion
Organic chemicals that contribute to smog formation
Secondary pollutant that affects human health
Toxic heavy metal emitted from industrial sources

body.text: Scheduled inspections and servicing of equipment are conducted to identify and rectify issues that may lead to inefficiencies or increased emissions, ensuring optimal performance and compliance with environmental standards.

rows: Check for scale build-up and operational efficiency
Assess air flow and contamination control

body.text: All emissions data from CEMS and laboratory results are documented, and regularly reviewed by the Environmental Compliance Officer and the Quality Assurance Team to ensure accuracy and compliance.

Advanced electrostatic dust suppression technology is utilized in areas with high dust generation i.e. manufacturing plant and material handling facilities.
Water sprays and dust suppressants are regularly applied during dust generating operations like grinding, Roll mill operations, surface preparation, material handling, cutting and slitting.
Dust levels are monitored regularly by environmental health and safety (EHS) personnel through continuous air quality monitoring systems (AQMS)
Employees receive training on best practices for dust control, including the use of personal protective equipment (PPE).

All company vehicles are maintained regularly to ensure efficient operation and low emissions, reducing the generation of pollutants such as SOx and NOx.
Low-emission vehicles, i.e. electric models, are integrated into the company fleet, significantly lowering Vehicular emissions.
Vehicle emissions are monitored regularly, and any non-compliant vehicles are repaired or replaced to maintain compliance with environmental standards.
Driver training includes fuel-efficient driving practices to minimize environmental impact, focusing on techniques that reduce emissions and fuel consumption.
All vehicles belonging to the company and employees must carry a valid Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificate to ensure compliance with emissions standards.

Employee transportation schedules are staggered by implementing varied start and end times for shifts, which helps spread out the flow of vehicles entering and exiting the facility. This approach minimizes the number of employees traveling during peak traffic hours, thereby reducing congestion and enhancing overall traffic management around the workplace
Carpooling and public transportation options are encouraged and supported by the company.
Delivery and logistics operations are planned by Logistics Manager in collaboration with the Operations Team to avoid rush hours, reducing the company's road congestion impact.
Company shuttle service is provided to further reduce the number of individual vehicles on the road.

Odour-generating processes such as chemical etching and electrolytic plating are enclosed, and Scubbers are installed to minimize emissions.
Activated carbon filters are used in ventilation systems to absorb and neutralize odorous compounds.
Regular maintenance of the odour control systems ensures they function optimally.
Odour levels are monitored regularly, and complaints are investigated and addressed immediately.
Employees are trained on odour control measures and proper handling of odourous materials.

Significant noise is generated by equipment such as rolling mills, shear machines, extruders, furnaces, ventilation fans, and pumps. To mitigate this noise and enhance safety, foam acoustic panels are installed around these machines, effectively reducing sound levels and minimizing noise pollution.
Regular maintenance ensures equipment operates within permissible noise levels.
Noise monitoring is conducted at regular intervals, with results reviewed by management.
Ear protection is provided to employees in high-noise areas, and its usage is mandatory.
Noise levels are documented, and any complaints or exceedances are investigated and rectified promptly by the Environmental Compliance Officer.

sops.title: Occupational Safety Risk and Incident Control Framework

blocks.text: To establish systematic procedures for identifying, assessing, and mitigating safety risks in the workplace, ensuring compliance with regulatory standards, and promoting a culture of safety to prevent incidents and protect the well-being of all employees.

body.text: Immediate Reporting: Employees must report any workplace safety incident or near-miss to the OH&S Supervisor immediately. Examples include slips, trips, falls, equipment malfunctions, and exposure to hazardous materials. Use the designated reporting channels: Email: incident.report@amwl.com Contact Person: OH&S Supervisor

Incident Documentation: The supervisor will document the incident using the Workplace Safety Incident Report Form, including details such as the date, time, location, persons involved, and a brief description of the incident.
Initial Response: The supervisor will take immediate steps to secure the area and prevent further incidents. This may include cordoning off the area, providing first aid, or shutting down equipment.

Conducting Risk Assessments: Annual risk assessments are conducted in all work areas to identify potential hazards. This includes evaluating the safety of machinery, tools, materials, and working conditions.
Risk Register: All identified risks are recorded in a Risk Register, with details on the nature of the risk, the likelihood of occurrence, potential impact, and control measures in place.

Implementation of Control Measures: Appropriate control measures are implemented to mitigate identified risks. This can include engineering controls, administrative controls, and personal protective equipment (PPE).
Incident Investigation Team: A team comprising members of the Safety Committee and relevant supervisors investigates all reported incidents.
Root Cause Analysis: The investigation team conducts a root cause analysis to identify underlying causes and contributing factors to the incident.
Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA): Based on the findings, the team recommends CAPAs to prevent recurrence. The implementation of these actions are tracked and documented.

Mandatory Safety Training: All employees must undergo safety training during onboarding and receive regular refresher courses. Topics covered will include hazard identification, safe work practices, and emergency response procedures.
Employees: Report any safety incidents or concerns immediately to the supervisor or Safety Officer. Follow all safety procedures and participate in safety training.
Supervisors/Department Heads: Ensure safety procedures are followed and report incidents to the Safety Officer. Conduct regular safety inspections and address any safety concerns.
Safety Supervisor: Assess and respond to reported incidents. Conduct risk assessments and implement safety measures. Maintain incident and training records.
Management: Review and approve safety procedures and protocols. Provide resources and support for safety initiatives.

blocks.text: This SOP will be reviewed by the Health and Safety Manager Every Two year or following any significant incident to ensure its continued relevance and effectiveness in maintaining workplace safety standards.

sops.title: Procedure for Compliance Approval of Sensitive Transactions

blocks.text: Establishes guidelines for obtaining approval and reporting and managing high-risk transactions, such as Charitable donations and sponsorships, procurement of goods and services, gifts, travel.

body.text: Sensitive transactions include: gifts, travel, entertainment, charitable donations, political contributions, and significant procurement activities. Determine if the type of transaction is sensitive. Confirm the type of transaction by reviewing the details, consulting with supervisor, seeking guidance from the Compliance Officer and hence document the findings.

Report to the Ethics Compliance officer for approval by meeting them in person or through email id: ethics.compliance@amwl.com. Provide context and purpose of the transaction. For transactions of significant value or risk, submit a formal request. On receival of approval document record the approval in the transaction file.
Maintain thorough records of the approved transaction. Include purpose, participants, expenses, and approval documentation. All records must accompany expense reports. Ensure all documents are filed.
Review the transaction for ethical implications post-approval. Ensure that the transaction is documented clearly and cannot be perceived as undue influence or bribery.
Verify that the transaction complies with company policies. Confirm that the transaction does not involve prohibited items such as loans, cash, personal checks, or gifts breaching laws.

sops.title: Procedure for Confidential Data Handling and Breach Responses

blocks.text: Defines procedures for managing confidential information, including data breach responses and protecting third-party data from unauthorized access or disclosure.

body.text: Data Classification: Data must be classified into three categories:

rows: Highly sensitive data requiring strict access controls e.g., personal information, financial records
Data that is important to the organization but not classified as confidential e.g., employee information, operational procedures
Information meant for public consumption e.g., marketing materials, press releases.

body.text: Access Control:

Access rights are assigned based on the principle of least privilege. The principle of least privilege (PoLP) refers to granting users only the access rights necessary to perform their job functions, minimizing the risk of unauthorized access or data breaches.
Roles and responsibilities are defined, and access is granted accordingly.
A quarterly review of access rights will be conducted by Data Protection Officer through automated access logs and reports, along with manual checks to ensure compliance with the established classifications. In case of non-compliance, access rights will be revoked, investigated, and corrective actions will be implemented, followed by a follow-up review to ensure compliance.

Confidential information are stored in secure environments e.g., locked file cabinets and secure servers such as cloud-based servers to guarantee encryption and regulatory compliance.
Transmission of confidential data is conducted via secure channels i.e. VPNs and encrypted emails.
All confidential data are encrypted both in transit and at rest, following industry-standard encryption protocols (e.g., AES-256).
Access to storage areas containing confidential data is restricted to authorized personnel.
Access control systems i.e. keycards is used to manage physical access.
Identification: For IT Department

System logs are records generated by operating systems, applications, or network devices that provide a detailed history of events, activities, and transactions occurring within a system
Regularly analyze system logs for unusual access patterns and failed login attempts to monitor for signs of data breaches.
Identification: For Employee

System logs are records generated by operating systems, applications, or network devices that provide a detailed history of events, activities, and transactions occurring within a system
Regularly analyze system logs for unusual access patterns and failed login attempts to monitor for signs of data breaches.
Reporting:

Employees must report any suspected data breaches immediately to their supervisor and the IT department.
An incident reporting form must be filled out and submitted to the IT department for documentation.
Escalation Protocol:
Depending on the severity, escalate incidents to management and legal counsel as necessary.

Containment: The IT Security manager will immediately isolate affected systems to prevent further unauthorized access. This team is responsible for implementing containment measures, which may include disconnecting the affected systems from the network, disabling user accounts, or restricting access until a thorough investigation is conducted and the issue is resolved.

Investigation: The Incident Response Team (IRT) will conduct a thorough investigation to determine the cause and impact of the breach. They will collect relevant logs and evidence, analyze data to identify vulnerabilities, and assess the breach's extent. Interviews with personnel may be conducted for additional insights. The team will document findings and prepare an incident report with recommendations for remediation. This approach helps prevent similar incidents in the future.

Communication: Affected stakeholders will be notified via email or formal communication channels, detailing the nature of the breach, affected data, and potential risks. Guidance will include recommended actions to protect their information, such as changing passwords and monitoring for suspicious activities. Regular updates will be provided as more information becomes available.

Internal Communication: Management and the legal team are kept informed through scheduled progress updates, including regular emails being sent on their respective official email-ids, meetings, and incident reports. All critical developments, decisions, and actions are documented and communicated in a timely manner to ensure alignment and compliance throughout the process.

Remediation: Corrective actions including revising data access controls, enhancing encryption protocols, updating security policies, providing targeted employee retraining, and improving incident detection systems are take. These measures are designed to address vulnerabilities identified during the investigation and prevent similar breaches in the future.

Post-Incident Review: A review meeting is conducted by the Incident Response Team, led by the IT Security Manager to analyze response effectiveness and identify improvements by enhancing communication protocols, refining the incident response process and upgrading security monitoring tools.
Documentation Retention: Maintain detailed records of the incident, including timelines, actions taken, and any communications for at least three years.

Regular Review: The IT Security Officer, will review and update the procedures annually or following significant incidents to ensure their effectiveness and alignment with evolving security threats and legal requirements

sops.title: Securing Third-Party Data from Unauthorized Access

blocks.text: To protect sensitive information shared with or received from third parties by implementing robust access controls, ensuring data privacy, and mitigating risks of unauthorized data exposure.

body.text: Access controls are implemented to ensure that only authorized personnel can access sensitive third-party data. Utilize Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) are considered to restrict access according to employees' job roles and responsibilities.

Third-party data is encrypted during transmission using secure protocols like SSL and at rest with industry-standard encryption algorithms (e.g., AES-256). Encryption keys are stored securely, granting access based on the need-to-know principle.
Third-party data are stored on secure, access-controlled encrypted servers and regular reviews of access permissions to ensure compliance with data protection policies are conducted

Third-party data are shared through secure methods such as encrypted email or secure file transfer protocols (SFTP). The identity and authorization of recipients are verified before sharing sensitive information, and maintain logs of all data-sharing activities, including recipient details and timestamps.

Third parties handling or accessing sensitive data have signed a Data Protection Agreement (DPA), outlining their obligations for safeguarding information. Contracts include clauses that mandate the implementation of equivalent security measures and the prompt reporting of any data breaches.

Regular training sessions are conducted for employees on data protection practices, including the proper handling and sharing of third-party data. Employees are aware of their responsibilities and the consequences of failing to protect third-party data.

Monitoring systems are in place to detect any unauthorized access or attempts to access third-party data. Regular audits of data access logs, storage practices, and third-party compliance are conducted to identify and rectify potential security gaps.

In case of a data breach involving third-party information, the Incident Response Procedure is followed to contain and mitigate the breach. Affected third parties are promptly notified, provided with breach details, potential impacts, and the corrective actions taken.

sops.title: Stakeholder Consent and Data Processing Retention and Disposal

blocks.text: To ensure that data is handled in compliance with stakeholder permissions, maintaining appropriate data retention periods and secure disposal practices to uphold privacy standards and regulatory requirements.

body.text: Consent is obtained through formal mechanisms through signed consent form and digital agreements. These documents clearly outline the purpose of data collection, how the data will be used, and stakeholders rights. Additionally, a confirmation process through email verification and electronic signature is used to ensure stakeholders have fully understood the terms before granting their consent.

Stakeholders are provided with clear information which is communicated through a Privacy Notice which outlines how data will be used, the retention periods, and the stakeholders rights regarding their data, including access, correction, or deletion. These documents are provided at the point of data collection, either in print or digital form.

Establishing Retention Timelines: Each type of data is categorized based on its sensitivity and relevance, with specific retention timelines defined according to legal requirements, business needs, or contractual obligations.

body.text: Tracking Retention Periods: Automated systems i.e. Microsoft SQL Server is utilized to track the retention period of stored data, ensuring that data is flagged for review or deletion once the retention period expires.

Secure Disposal: Once data is no longer required, it is securely deleted using methods appropriate to its sensitivity. For digital data, secure deletion methods such as data wiping or cryptographic erasure are used. For physical data, documents are shredded or incinerated in a controlled environment.
Compliance Checks: Regular audits are conducted to ensure that data is retained or disposed of in accordance with the established policies and legal requirements.

narrative.text: Regular Audits: The Data Protection Officer (DPO) will conduct the annual audits of data access and handling practices. The audit will be conducted through a systematic review process, including examining access logs, evaluating data handling procedures, interviewing relevant personnel, and assessing compliance with established policies. Additionally, random sampling of data access and handling activities may be performed to ensure adherence to standards.
Continuous Monitoring: Automated monitoring tool i.e Intrusion Detection System (IDS) to detect unauthorized access and anomalies in data access patterns.

sops.title: Procedure for Ethical Compliance Due Diligence Program for Third Parties

blocks.text: To assess and ensure that third-party entities adhere to ethical standards in areas such as anti-corruption, labor practices, environmental impact, and business integrity before and throughout their engagement with the organization.

body.text: The Compliance Officer conducts initial background checks on potential third parties, identifying any immediate ethical concerns or risk indicators. Third parties are screened against industry watchlists to detect any history of violations, including bribery or unethical practices. Information about their data protection policies, security measures, and compliance with applicable ethics laws is gathered.
The Compliance and Risk Management Team evaluates each third party's ethical practices across the following areas:

Anti-Corruption and Bribery: Policies are reviewed for compliance with anti-corruption regulations.
Labor Practices: Adherence to fair labor standards, ensuring no child or forced labor, is verified.
Environmental Responsibility: Environmental practices are evaluated for alignment with sustainability and protection standards.
Data Privacy and Information Security: Data handling policies are assessed to protect sensitive company and client information.
Human Rights and Fair Treatment: Commitment to human rights, diversity, equity, and inclusion is confirmed.
Health and Safety: Compliance with workplace safety and health protocols is ensured.
Relevant documentation is reviewed, including:

Data protection policies.
Security certifications (e.g., ISO 27001).
Contracts detailing data handling, sharing, and protection measures.
Potential risks are assessed based on:

The nature of the data accessed or processed.
The third party's security posture and compliance track record.
The geographic location and applicable data protection laws.

steps.heading: Approval Process

body.text:
Findings determine whether the third party meets the company's ethical standards.
Management approval is obtained from the senior management team, including the Data Protection Officer (DPO) based on the risk assessment findings before finalizing any contracts or agreements with the third party, requiring adherence to ethical standards with provisions for audits and penalties for violations
The approval process is documented for accountability.

steps.responsible: Senior management team; Data Protection Officer (DPO)

body.text: The performance and compliance of third-party vendors are regularly monitored through:

Scheduled audits and assessments.
Review of incident reports or security breaches.
Open communication is maintained with third parties to address compliance concerns or changes in their operations that may impact data protection.
Periodic reviews are conducted by the Data compliance officer to ensure ongoing compliance with contractual obligations and applicable data protection laws.

Third parties are required to report any data breaches or security incidents promptly.
A communication protocol for incident reporting and response is established.
Collaboration with third parties is undertaken to develop an incident response plan outlining roles, responsibilities, and procedures in case of a data breach.

Comprehensive records of all due diligence activities are maintained, including risk assessments, contracts, communication logs, and monitoring results.
Records are stored for a minimum of three years.

sops.title: Audits of Control Procedure to ensure Ethical Compliance

blocks.text: To ensure Ethical Compliance is to regularly assess and verify that ethical standards and controls are effectively implemented across operations, preventing non-compliance and fostering a culture of integrity.

body.text:
Audits are conducted bi-annually or after significant organizational changes.
The Audit Team schedules audits in advance and defines specific objectives and scope.

rows: Ensure accuracy of financial statements and compliance with accounting standards.
Review of financial records, transactions, and reporting practices.
Verify adherence to procurement policies and ethical vendor selection.
Examination of vendor contracts, processes, and compliance documentation.
Assess compliance with labor laws and internal policies regarding employee treatment. Evaluate fairness in hiring and employee practices.
Review of HR records, hiring practices, and employee feedback.
Evaluate truthfulness in advertising and compliance with marketing regulations.
Analysis of marketing materials and promotional activities.
Review adherence to internal policies and procedures across operations. Assess the effectiveness of operational processes.
Assessment of operational processes and compliance with standards.
Assess information security measures and data protection.
Evaluation of IT systems, access controls, and data management practices.
Identify and mitigate risks associated with corrupt practices and bribery incidents.
Review of compliance policies, employee training, and incident reports.

body.text:
The Audit Team reviews documentation and records related to the identified areas of ethics i.e. financial statements, vendor contracts, employee records.
Compliance with established ethical guidelines, policies, and regulatory requirements is assessed.
Interviews with key personnel are conducted to gain insights into ethical practices and any concerns.

The Audit Team analyzes collected data to identify trends, anomalies, and potential areas of ethical non-compliance.
Metrics and benchmarks are utilized to assess performance against ethical standards.

Audit findings are compiled into a detailed report that highlights compliance and non-compliance areas, along with recommendations for improvement.
The report is presented to management and relevant stakeholders for review.

An action plan is developed by the Audit Team in collaboration with relevant stakeholders, such as department heads and management representatives for addressing identified issues, detailing timelines and responsible parties.
Follow-up audits are scheduled to verify the implementation of corrective actions and assess ongoing compliance.

All audit records, including planning documents, evaluation results, reports, and follow-up actions, are maintained for a minimum of five years by the Audit Team in conjunction with the Compliance Department.

sops.title: Procedure for Employee Compliance and Awareness

blocks.text: To ensure that all employees are informed of, understand, and adhere to company policies and procedures, fostering a culture of compliance and accountability while promoting awareness of relevant regulations and ethical standards.

body.text: All employees are required to complete mandatory compliance training on data protection, confidentiality, and security protocols upon hiring and annually thereafter, covering topics like company data protection policies and recognizing phishing attacks.

Training materials, including handbooks are developed and distributed among the employes which contains all the relevant informations, ensuring they are regularly updated to reflect current laws and best practices.
Employees are trained on immediate reporting procedures, containment steps, and follow-up actions to take in the event of a data breach.

Periodic campaigns are conducted to reinforce data protection importance, utilizing newsletters, posters, and team meetings to share tips. Simulated phishing exercises are implemented to test employee awareness, with feedback provided to those who need improvement.
A culture that encourages reporting compliance concerns or suspicious activities without fear of retaliation is fostered. Reporting steps are clearly communicated to the employees.

Records of training completion and participation in awareness programs are maintained. The effectiveness of these programs is regularly evaluated through surveys and assessments, with adjustments made as necessary.

Regular audits are conducted by Data Protection Officer to assess adherence to data protection policies and employee training requirements. Findings are documented, and corrective actions are implemented as needed.

narrative.text: Regular audits will be conducted by the Data Protection Officer to ensure adherence to the SOPs and identify areas for improvement.; Participation in training programs will be tracked by the IT Manager, and employees must complete annual training to remain compliant.

blocks.text: Non-Compliance Consequences: Failure to comply with the SOPs may result in disciplinary actions taken by Human Resources Department in collaboration with IT Managers, which can include verbal warnings, written reprimands, suspension, or termination of employment, depending on the severity of the violation.

The SOP Manual will be reviewed annually by the Data Protection Officer to ensure relevance and compliance with current laws and best practices. Significant changes in regulations or operational processes will prompt emergency reviews. All revisions will be documented, and updated versions will be circulated to employees for acknowledgment.
